newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian security chiefs meet over plot charges.
newsitem.headline: Russian security chiefs meet over plot charges.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin met top security officials on Thursday to discuss accusations by the interior minister that security tsar Alexander Lebed was plotting to seize power.
RIA news agency said the defence and interior ministers, security service heads and President Boris Yeltsin's chief of staff met at nine a.m. (0500 GMT).
The agency made no mention of Lebed being at the meeting. He has denied the charges made by Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov on Wednesday and said there could be no talk of a coup d'etat in Russia.
"Let's all sleep quietly. I guarantee that nothing will happen," said Lebed, who has made many powerful enemies since being given the job of Security Council secretary in late June.

Kulikov accused Lebed of plotting a "creeping coup" while Yeltsin was preparing for heart surgery -- a charge which may force Yeltsin to choose between the minister and the security tsar. He called for an end to the squabbling on Tuesday.
Kulikov told a news conference on Wednesday that he had ordered extra security measures to cope with what he said was a threat of attacks by rebels from the breakaway Chechnya region.
"We have intelligence information that (Lebed) was promised that 1,500 (Chechen) gunmen would help him to power here in Moscow," said Kulikov.
Lebed has negotiated a peace deal with the Chechen separatists, ending 21 months of bloody fighting. But Kulikov and others have said the deal is tantamount to a capitulation by Moscow.

Yeltsin's press office said the president, who is being prepared for surgery at the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow, was worried by Kulikov's statement and had asked Chernomyrdin to get full details of the charges.
Kulikov said Lebed, who joined Yeltsin's team after coming a strong third in the first round of presidential polls in June, was planning to seize power without elections.
"(Lebed) has decided to move ahead using force instead of waiting for the next presidential poll," he said.

Lebed dismissed the minister's accusations. "There cannot even be talk of an attempted coup d'etat," he told a hastily-called news conference on Wednesday. "Nothing will happen...unless Kulikov stirs things up."
Lebed said he believed his rival would be fired over the incident.
Yeltsin's announcement on September 5 that he would undergo a heart operation fuelled the power struggle in the Kremlin.
The president moved slowly and his eyes looked puffy in brief television footage of a meeting on Wednesday with Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko.
Yeltsin suffered two heart attacks last year and one surgeon has said he may have had a third in the middle of this year.
The president has already delegated some powers to Chernomyrdin.

The drama overshadowed a visit to Moscow by U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry, designed to persuade parliament to ratify the START-2 treaty which would slash the number of strategic nuclear warheads to a third of Cold War levels.
Defence Minister Igor Rodionov said after talks with Perry that he hoped parliament would ratify the treaty. Perry was due to address the State Duma, the lower house of parliament, later on Thursday.
